content:
maria: FYI seeing a pile of 502/504s from user-facing proxy in us-east-1 starting ~10:04 UTC. Dashboard shows a big spike in connection errors and retries. 

devops-bot: [ALERT] High NAT SNAT port usage in us-east-1 (CloudWatch link) — 95% of ephemeral ports in use on nat-0a1b2c3d.

lee: Can you paste the netstat from one of the worker nodes? thinking TIME_WAIT buildup or client churn.

maria: grabbing it now. short snippet below from one host (10.0.45.12) — most lines are TIME_WAIT on 10.0.45.x: 
```
$ sudo ss -tanp | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l
> 37240
$ sudo ss -tan "sport = :1024..65535" | head -n 10
TIME-WAIT 0 0 10.0.45.12:40012 34.217.1.23:443 users:("nginx",pid=4212,fd=23)
TIME-WAIT 0 0 10.0.45.12:40013 34.217.2.11:443 users:("nginx",pid=4212,fd=24)
...
```

chris: Confirming — that's basically exhausting ephemeral ports on the NAT. CloudWatch SNATPortUtilization shows 96% for nat-0a1b2c3d. Are all public subnets routing to the same NAT?

anika: I pulled the terraform state for route tables. Looks like during the last subnet templating change we accidentally pointed two private subnet route tables (10.0.32.0/24 and 10.0.45.0/24) in different AZs to the same single NAT gw in us-east-1a (nat-0a1b2c3d) instead of their local az nat-0b2c3d4e.

lee: Oof. So cross-AZ traffic + single NAT = single SNAT pool hammered. That explains why one NAT is saturated even though we have spare NATs in other AZs.

maria: any quick mitigations we can do before change window? metrics still climb.

chris: Short-term mitigations (ranked):
1) Update route tables to point subnets back to their AZ-local NAT (fast, low risk if we do one subnet at a time).
2) If we need immediate relief, onboard an extra NAT gateway in the same AZ and swap routes for a few subnets (but still risk config drift).
3) Tune kernel on nodes: increase ephemeral port range and reduce TIME_WAIT (net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30, ip_local_port_range to 1024-65535) — only a stopgap and may not be allowed by policy.
4) Reduce egress churn: enable keepalive/persistent connections on upstream clients (nginx -> backend reuse).

anika: I'll prepare a small terraform diff to fix route_table associations. Can we do a canary: update 1 AZ first?

ops-sre: +1 on canary. We should also add a CloudWatch alarm for SNATPortUtilization > 80% with paging. Right now it only fires at 95%.

maria: netstat shows increased connection churn from our image pullers too — model-pull jobs are creating lots of short-lived TCP connections to external registries. We're going to throttle parallel pulls as well.

lee: For longer term: consider egress proxies (squid/nginx) in each AZ to pool connections, or move external registry traffic to a VPC endpoint or S3/registry mirror inside the VPC so it won't consume SNAT ports. Also document route table checks in infra runbook.

chris: I've started the terraform plan now for per-AZ route fix (only touching route-table-association for rt-abc123 -> nat-0b2c3d4e). will apply to us-east-1b first and monitor.

maria: applying to us-east-1b now (rolling, one subnet at a time). will watch CloudWatch. :eyes:

(devops-bot): Deploy started by chris: plan -> apply (link).

lee: While this rolls, set net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30 on a subset of autoscaling group instances? any objections?

anika: I'd rather not change kernel params cluster-wide. If we have to, do it on ephemeral nodes only and revert after.

ops-sre: alarm updated to 80% and paging enabled. Dashboard annotation added for the config change window.

maria: after updating 2 subnets in us-east-1b SNAT usage dropped from 96% -> 62% for nat-0a1b2c3d. errors in the proxy dropped too.

chris: Good. Finish route fixes for remaining AZs in the change window. Then follow-ups:
- Add infra unit test to ensure route tables point to same-AZ NATs.
- Add egress traffic memo: prefer VPC endpoints and mirrors for big external pulls.
- Add synthetic test that simulates high connection churn to detect port exhaustion.

maria: assigning follow-ups: anika -> route table unit test + terraform PR, lee -> egress proxy evaluation, ops-sre -> alarm + synthetic test. I'll keep this thread updated.

ops-sre: noted. scheduling a retro tomorrow to review the process and how the subnet templating change slipped through.

maria: thanks everyone. will close when metrics stable for 24h. :white_check_mark:
